Note::base64_decode¶

Back to Note API Reference

Signature¶

Note Note::base64_decode() const

Decode Every Cell From Base64¶

base64_decode() is the inverse of base64_encode: it reads each cell as standard Base64 (RFC 4648 alphabet, = padding) and replaces it with the decoded bytes. Use it to unpack values that were carried through an ASCII-only channel.

The decoded bytes are placed into a UTF-8-mode Note as-is; if the original data was text they read back as text, and if it was binary the cell simply holds those bytes. For anything that produced a Note with base64_encode(), this is an exact round trip.

Decoding is lenient: characters outside the Base64 alphabet are skipped rather than raising an error, and a cell that is not Base64 at all comes back best-effort (often unchanged). Do not rely on base64_decode() to validate input — check the shape of the data yourself if it matters. The operation is shape-preserving, cell-independent, and returns a fresh Note; an empty cell decodes to an empty cell.

Example 1: Decode A Batch¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::make_note({"SGVsbG8=", "Y2Fmw6k=", ""}).base64_decode())
    << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, encoding=utf8)
["Hello", "café", ""]

"Y2Fmw6k=" decodes to the five UTF-8 bytes of "café".

Example 2: Exact Round Trip¶

const pluss::Note original = pluss::make_note({"payload", "café"});
std::cout << original.base64_encode().base64_decode() << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[2], dim=1, numel=2, encoding=utf8)
["payload", "café"]

Example 3: Lenient On Non-Base64 Input¶

pluss::note::print(std::cout,
                   pluss::make_note({"not!!base64"}).base64_decode())
    << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[1], dim=1, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
["not!!base64"]

No exception — the input is returned best-effort.
